financials_interim.notes: RENUKA FOODS PLC COMPANY (standalone holding-company) basis, three months ended 30 June 2026. The Company earns essentially no operating revenue this quarter (printed '-', vs a small Rs.10,514k in Q1 FY2025/26) -- revenue/cost_of_sales/gross_profit left blank as immaterial/not meaningful, consistent with the GROUP row's holding-company convention. Operating result swung to a small Rs.(694)k LOSS from a Rs.2,300k profit YoY, driven by Administrative Expenses (Rs.8,235k to Rs.694k -- expenses actually fell, so this is not the loss driver) net against the loss of the small prior-year revenue base; PBT was carried instead by Finance Income of Rs.18,291k (nil in the prior-year quarter) to Rs.17,597k (2025: Rs.2,300k, +665%). PAT Rs.12,110k (2025: Rs.2,300k, +426%). EPS 0.03 (2025: 0.01); diluted EPS 0.06 (2025: 0.01) -- same basic-vs-diluted anomaly noted at GROUP level applies here (diluted exceeds basic), see GROUP row's notes. No borrowings at Company level (short_term_borrowings/long_term_borrowings stored as 0 -- Company SOFP carries no interest-bearing debt line).

Source: RENUKA FOODS PLC Interim Financial Statements for the period ended 30 June 2026 (filed CSE 11-Aug-2026). FYE 31 March. Income Statement p.3, SOFP p.4, Cash Flow p.6, Segment Analysis p.7, Operational Review (MD&A) p.2. GROUP basis. Q1 is both the 'Quarter Ended' and 'Period Ended' column since this is the first quarter of FY2026/27 -- both columns are identical in the filing; only the Quarter-ended column values are used here. tax_expense=56,341 and prior-year tax=0 were reconstructed by cross-checking PBT-PAT (273,534-217,192=56,342~56,341; 2025: 79,986-79,986=0) against the raw extracted 'Taxation' row, which the PDF text layer rendered with blank/zero cells omitted (a genuine extraction quirk, resolved by identity check, not guesswork). EPS ANOMALY FLAGGED: printed basic EPS (0.28, 2026; 0.43, 2025) is LOWER than printed diluted EPS (0.55, 2026; 0.43, 2025) for the current quarter -- diluted EPS exceeding basic EPS is inconsistent with normal LKAS 33 mechanics (dilution should never increase EPS) and could not be reconciled to any share count in the filing (basic ties exactly to total shares in issue -- 374,624,234 = 360,010,634 voting + 14,613,600 non-voting per Note 3 -- but 0.55 implies a denominator of ~192mn, roughly half, with no such share count disclosed anywhere); re-verified directly against word coordinates in the source PDF (not a column-swap on our part -- the filing itself prints 0.55 in the 'Diluted EPS' row). Both eps_basic and eps_diluted are stored exactly as printed, with this inconsistency flagged as a filing-level anomaly, not corrected. DRIVER 1 (segmental, p.7): Agri Food Exports segment swung from a Rs.(4,231)k LOSS to a Rs.86,379k PROFIT (a Rs.90,610k improvement); Consumer Brands segment profit grew Rs.46,596k (+55.3%, Rs.84,217k to Rs.130,813k). These two swings sum to exactly the Group PAT increase of Rs.137,206k (79,986 to 217,192) -- Agri Food Exports accounts for 66% of the improvement, Consumer Brands 34%. DRIVER 2 (income statement): Net Finance Income swung from a Rs.(97,284)k COST to a Rs.46,350k INCOME (a Rs.143,634k favourable swing), driven by Finance Income more than quadrupling (Rs.45,579k to Rs.203,593k, +346.7%; no explanation given in the filing for the surge -- a genuine disclosure gap, plausibly FX-translation gains on the Agri Food Exports segment's USD receivables given the segment's export orientation, but not confirmed) against a smaller rise in Finance Costs (Rs.142,863k to Rs.157,243k, +10.1%). PBT growth of Rs.193,548k (79,986 to 273,534) decomposes into operating-profit growth of Rs.49,914k (25.8%) plus the Rs.143,634k net-finance swing (74.2%) -- the finance-income surge is the LARGER of the two PBT drivers, not the segmental operating improvement. NOTABLE: despite Group PAT +171.5% (Rs.79,986k to Rs.217,192k), profit attributable to Owners of the Company grew only +28.2% (Rs.82,431k to Rs.105,675k) because Non-Controlling Interest swung from a Rs.(2,445)k LOSS-share to a Rs.111,518k PROFIT-share, capturing Rs.113,963k of the Rs.137,206k total PAT increase (83%) -- this NCI shift, not a change in underlying owner economics, is why basic EPS fell YoY (0.43 to 0.28) even as Group PAT surged. MD&A (p.2) confirms Group Revenue -1% YoY (Rs.3,798Mn to Rs.3,769Mn) with export mix falling from 45.5% to 43.0% of revenue (Export Revenue Rs.1,728,823k to Rs.1,618,083k, -6.4%; Domestic Revenue Rs.2,068,809k to Rs.2,150,535k, +3.9%, Segment Analysis p.7), and combined Admin+Selling expenses +11% YoY (Rs.474Mn to Rs.526Mn: Admin Rs.206,119k to Rs.202,613k -1.7%, Selling & Distribution Rs.268,104k to Rs.322,955k +20.5%). short_term_borrowings=4,020,798 (Current Portion of Interest Bearing Borrowings 3,899,304 + Bank Overdraft 121,494); long_term_borrowings=38,888 (non-current Interest Bearing Borrowings only; Lease Liabilities of 143,417 non-current / 7,966 current excluded as not classic debt). cash_and_equivalents=1,838,068 is the BS gross figure; CF statement's closing cash of 1,716,573 nets off the 121,494 Bank Overdraft (1,838,068-121,494=1,716,574~1,716,573) -- consistent, not a discrepancy. capex=204,578 is 'Acquisition of Property, Plant and Equipment / Investment Properties' only; a further Rs.20,135k was spent on Biological Assets (not included in the capex field).

thesis.thesis_text: Renuka Foods is a diversified food & beverage group split between a Consumer Brands segment and an export-oriented Agri Food Exports segment. Q1 FY2026/27 Group Revenue was roughly flat (-0.76% YoY to Rs.3,768.62mn) but gross margin expanded to 19.8% from 16.7%, and the Agri Food Exports segment swung from a Rs.4.23mn loss to an Rs.86.38mn profit -- a genuine, segment-identified operating turnaround that drove 66% of the Rs.137.21mn Group PAT increase, with Consumer Brands contributing the remaining 34% (+55.3% segment profit growth). However, the larger driver of the 242.1% PBT growth was actually a Rs.158.01mn (+346.7%) surge in Finance Income that the filing does not explain anywhere (74.2% of the PBT increase) -- plausibly FX-translation gains linked to the export segment, but unconfirmed. Critically, Non-Controlling Interest captured 83% of the total PAT increase, so profit attributable to Owners of the Company (the EPS basis) grew only 28.2%, and basic EPS actually FELL YoY to Rs.0.28 from Rs.0.43 -- a materially different picture from the 171.5% headline Group PAT growth. The stock trades at ~23.4x annualized P/E on this owners'-EPS basis, which is not cheap given flat revenue, real leverage (Rs.4.06bn of borrowings against Rs.9.40bn equity), and a filing-level EPS anomaly (diluted EPS of Rs.0.55 printed higher than basic EPS of Rs.0.28, unreconciled) (interim filed 11-Aug-2026, source_doc_id manual_cf3e0f5564d33684).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- renormalized across the remaining five pillars. Confidence is capped by having only one quarter of financials on file with no QoQ comparator (the prior local document was over 4 years stale, though CSE filing history confirms COCO files normally on the 45-day interim schedule). Two genuine, unresolved filing-level gaps materially limit confidence: (1) the Rs.158.01mn (+346.7%) YoY surge in Finance Income -- the largest single driver of PBT growth -- is not explained anywhere in the filing; (2) printed Diluted EPS (Rs.0.55) exceeds Basic EPS (Rs.0.28), an apparent computational inconsistency re-verified against the source PDF and not resolved. Both are treated as genuine uncertainties, not resolved facts, and should be queried directly with the company before treating this quarter's growth rate as a clean read on trading momentum.

financial_quality.rationale: Gross margin expanded to 19.8% from 16.7% and current ratio is adequate (~1.69x, current assets Rs.8,117.14mn / current liabilities Rs.4,801.18mn), but the group carries real debt (~Rs.4,059.69mn short+long-term borrowings against Rs.9,403.24mn equity, ~43% D/E) and the filing contains an unresolved EPS anomaly (diluted EPS of Rs.0.55 printed above basic EPS of Rs.0.28) that raises questions about the reliability of the per-share disclosures.

growth_outlook.rationale: Group Revenue was roughly flat (-0.76% YoY), and while the Agri Food Exports segment genuinely turned around (Rs.4,231k loss to Rs.86,379k profit) and Consumer Brands grew a steady +55.3%, the headline 171.5% PAT growth is inflated by a Rs.158,014k unexplained Finance Income surge and largely absorbed by Non-Controlling Interest -- owners'-EPS-relevant growth was only +28.2%, more representative of true underlying growth.

valuation.rationale: At Rs.26.2/share (market cap Rs.9.43bn), the stock trades at roughly book value but a moderately rich ~23.4x annualized P/E on owners'-attributable EPS, given flat revenue and the unresolved finance-income and EPS-anomaly questions -- not statistically cheap.

business_quality.rationale: Diversified food & beverage group with defined Agri Food Exports and Consumer Brands segments; the export segment turnaround is a genuine positive signal for franchise quality, though NCI captured 83% of this quarter's PAT increase, indicating the consolidated entity's minority structure meaningfully dilutes owners' share of growth.

governance_risk.rationale: Two unresolved filing-level issues -- an unexplained 346.7% surge in Finance Income (the largest single PBT driver) and a Diluted EPS figure (Rs.0.55) that exceeds Basic EPS (Rs.0.28), inconsistent with normal dilution mechanics -- were both re-verified against the source PDF and remain unreconciled, a genuine governance/disclosure-quality concern.

key_reasons: Agri Food Exports segment genuinely turned around, swinging from a Rs.4,231k loss to an Rs.86,379k profit YoY, and gross margin expanded to 19.8% from 16.7%
Consumer Brands segment profit grew a steadier +55.3% YoY to Rs.130,813k, providing some diversification of the earnings improvement beyond the export swing

Group carries real debt (~Rs.4.06bn) but current ratio remains adequate (~1.69x) and the company retains a dividend history (FY2023 DPS Rs.0.41), though no dividend has been declared in the two most recent years on file
watch_factors: Owners'-attributable EPS actually FELL YoY (Rs.0.43 to Rs.0.28) even as headline Group PAT grew 171.5%, because Non-Controlling Interest captured 83% of the total PAT increase -- the headline growth rate materially overstates the improvement in per-share economics

Finance Income surged 346.7% YoY (Rs.158,014k), the single largest driver of PBT growth (74.2%), with no explanation given anywhere in the filing -- a genuine, unresolved uncertainty that should not be treated as a repeatable operating gain

The filing prints Diluted EPS (Rs.0.55) higher than Basic EPS (Rs.0.28) for this quarter, which is inconsistent with normal dilution mechanics and could not be reconciled to any disclosed share count -- a filing-quality red flag worth raising directly with the company

horizon_notes.6m: Q2 FY2026/27 results will show whether the Agri Food Exports turnaround and the unexplained Finance Income surge both persist, or whether the finance-income jump was quarter-specific.
horizon_notes.1y: If Agri Food Exports sustains profitability and owners'-EPS growth converges toward the segment-level improvement (~28-55%) rather than the inflated headline PAT growth, the ~23.4x multiple would need continued earnings delivery to be justified.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on whether the export segment turnaround reflects a durable shift in COCO's product/export mix or a one-off pricing/FX benefit, and on how NCI's growing share of consolidated profit affects owners' returns going forward.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/industry data source in this project to assess global commodity/export-food demand cycles or currency trends relevant to COCO's Agri Food Exports segment.

interim_updates.note_text: Renuka Foods PLC (COCO) reported Group Revenue of Rs.3,768,619k for the quarter ended 30 June 2026, -0.76% YoY (2025: Rs.3,797,632k; MD&A, p.2, rounds this to '-1%'), with export sales falling to 43% of Group revenue from 45.5% PY (Export Revenue Rs.1,618,083k vs Rs.1,728,823k, -6.4%; Domestic Revenue Rs.2,150,535k vs Rs.2,068,809k, +3.9%, Segment Analysis p.7). By segment (p.7): Agri Food Exports swung from a Rs.(4,231)k LOSS to a Rs.86,379k PROFIT (a Rs.90,610k improvement, 66% of the Group's total Rs.137,206k PAT increase); Consumer Brands profit grew a steadier +55.3% YoY to Rs.130,813k (2025: Rs.84,217k, contributing the remaining 34% of the PAT increase). Group Gross Profit margin expanded to 19.8% from 16.7% PY (Rs.745,527k/Rs.3,768,619k vs Rs.635,517k/Rs.3,797,632k), but combined Admin+Selling expenses rose 11% YoY to Rs.526mn (2025: Rs.474mn; MD&A, p.2) -- Selling & Distribution Expenses alone rose 20.5% (Rs.268,104k to Rs.322,955k) while Administrative Expenses fell 1.7% (Rs.206,119k to Rs.202,613k), so Group Operating Profit grew a more modest +28.16% YoY to Rs.227,184k (2025: Rs.177,270k). The LARGER driver of PBT growth was actually below the operating-profit line: Net Finance Income swung from a Rs.(97,284)k COST to a Rs.46,350k INCOME (a Rs.143,634k favourable swing, 74.2% of the total Rs.193,548k PBT increase), on Finance Income more than quadrupling YoY (Rs.45,579k to Rs.203,593k, +346.7%, UNEXPLAINED in the filing -- a genuine disclosure gap, plausibly FX-translation gains on the Agri Food Exports segment's USD receivables given the segment's export orientation, but not confirmed). Group PBT grew 242.1% YoY to Rs.273,534k (2025: Rs.79,986k); Income Tax Expense of Rs.56,341k was incurred this quarter versus a NIL tax charge in Q1 FY2025/26. Group PAT grew 171.5% YoY to Rs.217,192k (2025: Rs.79,986k) -- but Owners-of-the-Company profit (the basis for EPS) grew only +28.2% YoY (Rs.82,431k to Rs.105,675k) because Non-Controlling Interest's share swung from a Rs.(2,445)k LOSS-share to a Rs.111,518k PROFIT-share, capturing Rs.113,963k (83%) of the total PAT increase; basic EPS consequently FELL YoY to Rs.0.28 from Rs.0.43 despite the large headline PAT growth. A filing-level anomaly is flagged: printed Diluted EPS (Rs.0.55) exceeds printed Basic EPS (Rs.0.28) for this quarter, which is inconsistent with normal LKAS 33 mechanics and could not be reconciled to any disclosed share count -- stored as printed, not corrected. COMPANY (standalone holding company) level: near-zero revenue (Rs.10,514k in 2025, nil in 2026), with the quarter's Rs.12,110k PAT (2025: Rs.2,300k) driven almost entirely by Finance Income of Rs.18,291k (nil PY).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: COCO's prior on-file document (dated 2022-05-31, covering the period ended 31 March 2022) was over 4 years stale before this refresh -- the CSE API shows this 30 June 2026 quarter filed on schedule (11-Aug-2026, within the standard 45-day interim filing window), confirming COCO is an actively trading, actively disclosing company; the multi-year local staleness was purely a sourcing gap on this platform, NOT suspension, delisting risk, or non-disclosure by the company. No closer prior quarter has yet been entered into financial_statements/interim_updates to support a QoQ comparison, only this fresh entry. Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) the Rs.158,014k (+346.7%) YoY surge in Finance Income -- the single largest driver of PBT growth (74.2% of the increase) -- is not explained anywhere in the filing (no MD&A commentary beyond the brief Operational Review on p.2, which covers only revenue/expenses/PAT/EPS at headline level, not the finance-income line); (2) the printed Diluted EPS (Rs.0.55) exceeding Basic EPS (Rs.0.28) for the current quarter is an apparent filing-level computation inconsistency -- re-verified directly against word-level PDF coordinates (not a column-extraction artifact on our part) and could not be reconciled to any share count disclosed in the filing; both figures stored as printed with this flagged; (3) the 'Taxation' row in the raw PDF text layer omitted its zero/blank cells (2025 tax = nil), reconstructed via the PBT-tax=PAT identity, not assumed; (4) no qualitative explanation is given for the Agri Food Exports segment's swing from loss to profit (Rs.90,610k improvement) beyond the segment-level figures themselves -- plausibly linked to the export/domestic revenue mix shift and/or the finance-income surge if that surge is FX-related, but this is inference, not disclosed fact.
interim_updates.takeaway: COCO's headline Group PAT growth of 171.5% YoY overstates the improvement in owners' economics: EPS-relevant profit (attributable to Owners of the Company) grew only 28.2%, because Non-Controlling Interest captured 83% of the total PAT increase -- basic EPS actually FELL YoY to Rs.0.28 from Rs.0.43. The largest single driver of the PBT surge was a Rs.158,014k (+346.7%) jump in Finance Income, which the filing does not explain and which is larger in Rupee terms than the genuine operating turnaround in the Agri Food Exports segment (Rs.90,610k swing from loss to profit). Revenue itself was roughly flat (-0.76% YoY), so this is a margin/segment-mix and finance-income story, not a volume story; the unexplained finance-income jump and the basic-vs-diluted EPS inconsistency (0.28 vs 0.55) are both worth querying directly with the company before treating this quarter's growth rate as a clean read on trading momentum. COCO's multi-year filing gap on this platform was a sourcing issue only -- the company filed this quarter on the normal CSE 45-day interim schedule.
operational_highlights: Group Revenue Rs.3,768,619k, -0.76% YoY (2025: Rs.3,797,632k); Group Operating Profit Rs.227,184k, +28.16% YoY; Group PBT Rs.273,534k, +242.1% YoY; Group PAT Rs.217,192k, +171.5% YoY.

Agri Food Exports segment swung from a Rs.(4,231)k LOSS to a Rs.86,379k PROFIT (Rs.90,610k swing, 66% of the Group PAT increase); Consumer Brands segment profit +55.3% YoY to Rs.130,813k (34% of the increase).
Finance Income more than quadrupled YoY, Rs.45,579k to Rs.203,593k (+346.7%) -- the largest single driver of PBT growth (74.2% of the Rs.193,548k increase), with no explanation given in the filing.

Non-Controlling Interest captured 83% (Rs.113,963k) of the Group's total PAT increase, swinging from a Rs.(2,445)k loss-share to a Rs.111,518k profit-share -- basic EPS FELL YoY (Rs.0.43 to Rs.0.28) despite Group PAT growing 171.5%.
Export sales mix fell to 43% of Group revenue from 45.5% PY (Export Revenue -6.4% YoY to Rs.1,618,083k; Domestic Revenue +3.9% YoY to Rs.2,150,535k).
Combined Admin+Selling expenses +11% YoY to Rs.526mn, driven by Selling & Distribution Expenses +20.5% YoY (Rs.268,104k to Rs.322,955k); Administrative Expenses actually fell 1.7%.
key_drivers: Agri Food Exports segment turnaround (Rs.(4,231)k loss to Rs.86,379k profit, a Rs.90,610k swing) is the dominant operating-level driver, 66% of the Group PAT increase.

Finance Income surge of Rs.158,014k YoY (+346.7%), unexplained in the filing, is the single largest PBT-level driver (74.2% of the total PBT increase) -- larger than the combined operating-profit improvement.

Non-Controlling Interest absorbed 83% of the total PAT increase, meaning owners' (EPS-relevant) profit grew only 28.2% even as Group PAT grew 171.5% -- a minority-interest dilution effect, not a change in underlying Group economics.

_gaps: ebitda: depreciation_amortization not disclosed; EBITDA understated (= operating profit only)
